correctness.rationale: Stable color equality gives isomorphic rooted universal covers. In a unicyclic graph the universal cover is a periodically decorated bi-infinite path, whose spine is intrinsic and therefore preserved by every automorphism. The induced translation/reflection of the spine descends to a dihedral symmetry of the unique finite cycle, and the finite rooted decoration isomorphisms glue to a graph automorphism. Thus stable colors coincide exactly with automorphism orbits. The tree case follows because its universal cover is the tree itself. The explicit bicyclic obstruction has an equitable degree partition strictly coarser than its orbit partition.

evidence: Arvind--Köbler--Rattan--Verbitsky define refinable graphs and explicitly note the tree case; full-text searches return no occurrence of unicyclic or pseudoforest.

Kiefer--Schweitzer--Selman prove orbit recovery for C^2-identified graphs, but explicitly note that cycles of length at least six are not C^2-identified, so their theorem does not imply the present unicyclic result.
Krebs--Verbitsky prove that round-r colors are exactly depth-r rooted universal-cover types; they do not state the descent property for unicyclic universal covers.

value.rationale: Refinability is a named level in the standard color-refinement hierarchy. The theorem gives a complete natural class guarantee at cyclomatic number one, extends the classical tree phenomenon to all connected unicyclic graphs, sharply separates cycle rank one from cycle rank two, and distinguishes orbit recovery from the narrower amenability/C^2-identification property.
